Package io.github.mikestitt.corbelsflightlog

Class FlightLog

java.lang.Object
io.github.mikestitt.corbelsflightlog.FlightLog
public final class FlightLog extends Object
One WPILOG file per OpMode run, for AdvantageScope.

Files are named <run>-<date>-<time>.wpilog in directory (logs by default). On an FTC robot, corbelsflightlog-ftc points that at /sdcard/FIRST/logs. Open the files with AdvantageScope.

Only changes are written. Each channel remembers the last value it wrote and skips a call whose value is identical. AdvantageScope holds a value until the next record, so nothing is lost -- a boolean that's true for the whole match is one record, not one per loop. The exception is event(java.lang.String), which records every call, since two identical events are two things that happened.

Never throws into the OpMode. If the file can't be opened or a write fails, logging switches itself off and status() says why.

One type per channel. A channel's type is fixed by its first value. A later call with a different type is ignored, and a one-time note is added to /Events so it's easy to spot.

Pose frame. Pose methods take Pedro coordinates (inches, origin in a field corner, radians) and write WPILib Pose2d structs in the frame AdvantageScope's FTC fields use: meters, origin at field center, turned by fieldQuarterTurns -- VERIFY that turn for your season.

  • Field Details

    • directory

      public static File directory
      Where log files go. Public so tests can point it at a temp folder. On a robot, corbelsflightlog-ftc sets this to the Robot Controller's own storage.

    • maxDirectoryBytes

      public static long maxDirectoryBytes
      How much of directory logs may occupy. At open(java.lang.String), the oldest .wpilog files are deleted until the total is under this. Without it the folder grows until the device fills and logging stops.

    • fieldQuarterTurns

      public static int fieldQuarterTurns
      Counter-clockwise quarter turns from Pedro's axes to AdvantageScope's FTC axes. Display only -- nothing on the robot reads it.

      1 is verified for BIOBUZZ (2026-2027). To check it for another season, log a circle around the middle of the field and look at the four axis crossings: Pedro (96,72,90deg) should draw right of centre facing up, (72,96,180deg) above centre facing left, (48,72,270deg) left of centre facing down, (72,48,0deg) below centre facing right. Each crossing has a distinct position and heading, so a wrong turn or a mirrored axis shows up at once -- which the shape of the circle alone would not reveal.

    • mirrorTo

      public void mirrorTo(Nt4Server server)
      Sends every value this log records to server as well, under the same name and type, so AdvantageScope shows live what the file holds afterwards. Sends the struct schemas, and the last value of every channel already written, at once. Nothing is sent once the log stops recording. null stops mirroring.

    • pose

      public void pose(String key, double xIn, double yIn, double heightIn, double headingRad)
      A Pedro pose lifted off the floor, drawn on AdvantageScope's 3D field.

      Takes the same Pedro coordinates as pose(java.lang.String, double, double, double) -- inches, corner origin, radians -- plus a height in inches, and applies the same fieldQuarterTurns rotation. Use this rather than converting by hand: a 3D pose built from raw metres will sit at a different place on the field than the 2D one, which is exactly the bug it replaces.

    • poses

      public void poses(String key, double[] xyh)
      Several Pedro poses -- a path, a list of targets -- as one Pose2d[], which AdvantageScope draws as a trajectory. The array is {x0, y0, heading0, x1, y1, heading1, ...} in Pedro inches and radians. An empty array clears it. Skipped if any value is non-finite.

    • fieldPose

      public static double[] fieldPose(double xIn, double yIn, double headingRad)
      A Pedro pose in AdvantageScope's field frame, as {x, y, headingRad}.

      Takes the same arguments as pose(java.lang.String, double, double, double): inches from a field corner and radians counter-clockwise. Returns metres from the centre of the field, turned by fieldQuarterTurns, which is what this library writes for every converting call.

      Here so that code drawing the same robot somewhere this library does not write -- over NetworkTables, say -- converts the way the log does instead of repeating the arithmetic. Repeating it is how a 3D pose once came out 90 degrees from the 2D one; see PedroPose3dTest.
